title: Bitcoin and ether decline as stablecoin and licensing programs advance; portfolio at $141,650
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $83,860, down 0.6% over 24 hours, while ether fell 1.3% to about $2,696. The broader market was weaker: CoinGecko measured a 2.9% decline in total crypto market capitalization. Bitcoin held up better than ether, but neither escaped the pullback.

The latest US session brought some relief in oil and government bonds after a sharp rise in Treasury yields. Longer-dated yields reached multidecade highs before retreating, while improving Middle Eastern export flows helped ease oil prices. Elevated yields remain a difficult backdrop for speculative assets because safer debt offers greater competition for capital. That is a risk factor, rather than proof of what caused each crypto move.

Alloya and its subsidiary Appex launched a controlled pilot of CUUSD, an institutional dollar stablecoin on Ethereum. Appex minted one million tokens for testing, representing $1 million in digital value. Access is limited to approved institutions, with no consumer offering. The pilot gives credit unions a concrete way to test blockchain payments and settlement, although wider commercial use still depends on regulatory and supervisory requirements.

Ethereum infrastructure also moved forward with the release of Nimbus 26.9.0. Its developers classify the update as urgent for Sepolia operators ahead of the October 6 Glamsterdam activation. The release schedules that fork, improves synchronization and fixes a potential validator-slashing issue involving malicious beacon nodes. This is a practical software-readiness step for the testnet upgrade; it does not establish a mainnet activation date.

In the UK, the FCA authorization application window opens today under its published timetable for the new crypto regime. The covered activities include trading platforms, custody, staking arrangements and qualifying stablecoin issuance. The regime takes effect in October 2027, giving affected firms a preparation period. Opening applications advances the licensing process while leaving firms responsible for assessing which permissions their activities require.

Our portfolio is worth about $141,650, split between $13,368 in the active treasury and $128,282 in the cold-storage Safe. That is a $2,369, or 1.6%, mark-to-market decline from the previous comparable snapshot. The Safe still holds 26.74 million ARC directly, worth $108,310 and roughly 76% of the portfolio. Its $2,335 valuation decline explains nearly all of the overall decrease. Two WETH/ARC pools add $17,231 of combined exposure, so ARC concentration remains the dominant portfolio risk.

Other positions include $4,875 of cbETH, $1,827 in Beefy's USDC/cbMEGA pool and $546 on Hyperliquid. Aave holds $9,196 of supplied WETH against $2,925 of USDC debt across both wallets, with health factors of 3.34 and 2.22. Fluid is only $153 net, but its $1,056 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
